name: JPA + Flyway
description: Spring Data JPA (Hibernate) with hand-written Flyway migrations on PostgreSQL, for Spring Boot.

specSections.title: Data Model & Migrations
specSections.guidance: For each entity/table: columns with types, lengths and numeric precision, nullability and defaults; the primary key (UUIDv7 or identity); foreign keys with an explicit on-delete behaviour; unique indexes from business rules (say which are case-insensitive); check constraints; indexes for foreign keys and query predicates; enums stored as strings; UTC timestamps; and which aggregates are edited concurrently and need a concurrency token (409 CONFLICT). Then the migration plan: one migration per change, named, in order, with which steps are expand/contract (add, backfill, switch code, drop later) so the previous version keeps working during rollout; any data backfill; the reference/seed data (dev-only seed per role and state); and how migrations run in each environment (Flyway run by a migrate-only profile of the app image as the platform's pre-deploy step; ddl-auto=validate everywhere).

order.reason: Migrations come before the repositories, services and controllers that use their tables.

exclusive.reason: The data engineer owns migrations and entities, not endpoints or DTOs.

protectedPaths.reason: Versioned Flyway migrations on the base commit are immutable (FR-125, Flyway checksums); a schema change is a new V<n>__ file. Repeatable R__ migrations may change.

requiredEnv.description: PostgreSQL connection for the API. A postgres:// URI (Render, Railway ${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}, the Supabase session pooler, or External), converted at startup by an EnvironmentPostProcessor into spring.datasource url/username/password with sslmode=require; the migrate profile reads it the same way.

checklist.item: Exactly one new migration per schema change, never an edit to a migration that exists on the base commit.
Breaking changes (rename, drop, type change) use expand/contract so the previous version runs against the new schema during preview and production rollout.
Columns are explicit (lengths, precision, nullability), foreign keys have a deliberate on-delete, and every foreign key and query predicate is indexed.
Uniqueness rules from the spec are unique indexes or constraints (case-insensitive where the spec says so), and concurrently edited aggregates have a concurrency token mapped to 409 CONFLICT.
Timestamps are UTC (timestamptz/datetimeoffset) from an injected clock, and enums are stored as strings.
Integration tests run against the real engine in a container with every migration applied; no in-memory or SQLite substitute.
Queries are parameterised, project only the needed columns, paginate lists and avoid N+1.
The seed is idempotent, dev-only and gated; reference data is part of the migrations.
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto is validate (never update/create/create-drop outside test config) and spring.jpa.open-in-view is false.
Migrations are V<n>__<description>.sql with the next free version; CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY is alone in a non-transactional migration.
Entities map columns explicitly, use LAZY relationships with entity graphs or join fetches, @Version on concurrent aggregates, EnumType.STRING and Instant/OffsetDateTime.
Production runs Flyway as the one-off migrate step (migrate profile), with spring.flyway.enabled=false in the serving profile when there is more than one replica.
